title: Session fingerprinting + compact tamper-resistant audit trail for RBACv2 and SAML flows
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Close a pen-test-identified replay/weak-audit vector for administrative SSO flows by (1) introducing a session fingerprint bound to SAML assertions and transport attributes, and (2) creating a compact, append-only audit record format with tamper-evidence (Merkle root anchoring) so admin actions are provably auditable without blowing up retention costs. Background: Recent external pen-test (report linked) showed viable assertion replay and gaps in our audit trail that made event correlation difficult across multi-region Dedicated customers. This ticket implements the engineering changes, test harness, and rollout controls. Decisions made so far: - Use an HMAC-based session fingerprint computed over SAML assertion ID + TLS client/server 5-tuple + user agent hash + short random nonce, rotated on reauth. Keeps server-side state minimal. - Session tokens remain short-lived (15m) and refresh requires presenting the prior fingerprint and live SAML assertion binding. - Audit records emitted as newline-delimited canonicalized JSON with fields: timestamp, actor_id, session_fingerprint_hash, action_type, resource, spec_hash, prev_hash, signature. We will store only the root hashes in high-retention store; full records are in cost-optimized cold storage. - Anchor Merkle roots hourly in the audit service and mirror to an immutable blob (S3 with object lock) and push root summaries to the Security Slack channel. - Use KMS asymmetric signing keys (customer-managed for Private deployments) for audit signatures. Progress updates: - 2025-02-20: Threat model completed; attack trees added to Confluence (link below). Identified mitigations for assertion replay, compromised session tokens, and cross-region event correlation gaps. - 2025-02-24: PoC for session fingerprint HMAC landed (GH PR: GH-rlw/session-fingerprint-poc). PoC shows false-positive reauth rate <0.5% in dev traffic. - 2025-02-26: Audit schema v1 approved by Security and Compliance; kept compact to reduce tokenization while preserving essential forensics. - 2025-02-28: Integration tests for SAML refresh flow in CI added (GH PR: GH-rlw/saml-fingerprint-integration). Test flakiness addressed by normalizing UA strings server-side. - 2025-03-01: Pen-test remediation plan uploaded; awaiting Security review sign-off for rollout gating. Remaining work: - Implement rotation logic and token refresh path in runtime (code change). - Wire audit emitter into admin APIs and Dedicated control plane. - Implement Merkle root generator and periodic anchorer with retries + observability. - Add e2e replay simulations and high-volume audit load test. - Prepare migration for existing sessions (graceful expiry + forced reauth window). Rollout plan: Canary to internal-only tenant group (1% of traffic) for 48h -> Expand to Dedicated customers on reserved window -> Private deployments optional docs + scripts for key config. Rollback plan: Disable fingerprint check and accept legacy tokens for short window, but keep audit emission to avoid data loss. Acceptance criteria and test plan below.
acceptance_criteria: No remaining high or critical findings in follow-up pen-test for SSO/session replay vector
Integration e2e tests cover assertion replay, token rotation, cross-region correlation scenarios
Audit stream produces hourly Merkle root with successful anchoring >99.9% of runs in canary
Observed false-positive reauth rate <= 1% in canary over 48h
Documentation updated for Dedicated and Private (KMS key instructions) and Console shows audit root status per-tenant
